# MonoDreams Block-Based Distribution — Package Definition

## Context

MonoDreams has matured to the point where the engine surface is broad
(rendering, camera, collision, physics, hierarchy/transform, cursor,
level loading via two parsers, plus dialogue/UI/layout polish in
Examples) but everything ships as a single library. That works for
the in-repo example game, but doesn't scale to the goal of an
AI-friendly, modular, opinionated framework.

The goal is a **shadcn-style code-distribution** experience: users
install MonoDreams via a CLI that copies source files into their
project. They own the code; they can read it, modify it, and let AI
agents edit it directly without indirection. No opaque NuGet, no
inheritance gymnastics, no reflection or auto-config.

Compared to the prior-conversation reference: we are choosing the
*foundation-as-a-block* variant (option 1), not the *thin NuGet +
copyable rest* variant (option 2). This keeps the system uniform —
every piece is visible code in the user's repo — which is the trait
that most helps AI agents reason about and modify the engine.

This plan defines the **package set, their boundaries, and their
dependency graph**. It does *not* design the CLI or the registry
schema yet — those are follow-ups once the package boundaries
themselves are agreed.

## Package List (15 blocks)

The naming convention is lowercase kebab-case. Each block is a
self-contained directory of source files plus a `block.json` manifest
(schema TBD in a follow-up).

### 1. `foundation` — required, installed by `monodreams init`

The minimum every project needs. After `monodreams init` the user has
a runnable empty MonoGame window with an ECS world, screen
controller, transform/hierarchy systems, input abstractions, and the
debug logger.

**Files** (from `MonoDreams/`):
- `Screen/GameScreen.cs`, `Screen/ScreenController.cs`
- `State/GameState.cs`, `State/EntityHierarchy.cs`, `State/Logger.cs`
- `Component/Transform.cs`, `Component/ChildOf.cs`,
  `Component/EntityInfo.cs`
- `System/HierarchySystem.cs`, `System/TransformCommitSystem.cs`,
  `System/SizeSystem.cs`
- `Input/AInputState.cs`, `Input/InputReplayPlan.cs`
- `System/Input/AbstractInputHandlingSystem.cs`,
  `System/Input/InputReplaySystem.cs`
- `Message/PositionChangeMessage.cs`, `Message/SizeChangeMessage.cs`
- `Extension/EntityHierarchyExtensions.cs`,
  `Extensions/Monogame/RectangleExtensions.cs`
- `EntityFactory/IEntityFactory.cs` (the contract — used everywhere)
- `Util/RelativeReferential.cs`, `Util/Texture2DExtensions.cs`

**Why bundled, not split:** Transform without Hierarchy is broken
(per `docs/hierarchy-transform/premises.md` — `Transform.Parent` is a
matrix link, `ChildOf` is the lifecycle link, and
`TransformCommitSystem` must run for `Delta` to be valid downstream).
Input replay is bundled because every project will want headless
replay testing per `docs/CORE_TENETS.md` debug tenet.

---

### 2. `rendering` — depends on `foundation`

The core draw stack with sprites as the default draw type. Sprites
are what 90% of 2D MonoGame games need.

**Files:**
- `Component/Draw/DrawComponent.cs`, `SpriteInfo.cs`, `Visible.cs`
- `Draw/DrawLayerMap.cs`
- `System/Draw/MasterRenderSystem.cs`, `SpritePrepSystem.cs`,
  `CullingSystem.cs`, `YSortSystem.cs`, `FinalDrawSystem.cs`
- `Renderer/ViewportManager.cs`
- The three `RenderTargetID` values (Main, UI, HUD) — per
  `docs/rendering/premises.md`

---

### 3. `rendering-mesh` — depends on `rendering`

Add-on for shape rendering (used by the `InfiniteRunner` example for
the treadmill, player, charms, obstacles, and by the UI block for
button outlines).

**Files:**
- `Draw/IMeshGenerator.cs`, `Draw/MeshData.cs`
- `System/Draw/MeshPrepSystem.cs`
- A `Generators/` folder with the canonical filled-rectangle and
  circle generators (currently in Examples — promote)

---

### 4. `rendering-text` — depends on `rendering`

Static text rendering via SpriteFont.

**Files:**
- `Component/Draw/` text-info struct (split out of current
  TextPrepSystem if needed)
- `System/Draw/TextPrepSystem.cs`
- `System/Draw/TextUpdateSystem.cs` (only the static-update portion;
  the reveal logic moves to the next block)

---

### 5. `text-dynamic-reveal` — depends on `rendering-text`

The typewriter / character-by-character reveal effect.

**Files:**
- `Component/Draw/DynamicText.cs`
- The dynamic-reveal portion of the current `TextUpdateSystem`
  (split during migration)

---

### 6. `camera` — depends on `rendering`

Game-world camera with follow behavior.

**Files:**
- `Component/Camera.cs`, `Component/CameraFollowTarget.cs`
- `System/Camera/CameraFollowSystem.cs`

**Why a separate block:** Per `docs/CORE_TENETS.md`,
`CameraFollowSystem` is optional — some games want manual camera
control. Rendering compiles without it because `MasterRenderSystem`
queries the `Camera` component directly.

---

### 7. `physics` — depends on `foundation`

Velocity-driven motion and gravity. Can be used without `collision`
(e.g., parallax backgrounds, falling decorations).

**Files:**
- `Component/Physics/RigidBody.cs`, `Velocity.cs`
- `System/Physics/GravitySystem.cs`, `VelocitySystem.cs`

---

### 8. `collision` — depends on `foundation`; *integrates with*
`physics` when both present

Both AABB (`BoxCollider`) and SAT (`ConvexCollider`) ship together
because the detection and resolution systems handle both
polymorphically. Splitting them would tear apart the unified
`ColliderTag` query that the docs name as canonical.

**Files:**
- `Component/Collision/BoxCollider.cs`, `ConvexCollider.cs`,
  `ICollider.cs`, `ColliderTag.cs`
- `System/Collision/TransformCollisionDetectionSystem.cs`,
  `TransformCollisionResolutionSystem.cs`,
  `TransformPhysicalCollisionResolutionSystem.cs`,
  `CreateCollisionMessageDelegate.cs`
- `Message/CollisionMessage.cs`, `ICollisionMessage.cs`,
  `RigidBodyTouchMessage.cs`
- `Extensions/Monogame/SATCollision.cs`,
  `Extensions/Monogame/CollisionRect.cs`

**Soft dep on physics:** `TransformPhysicalCollisionResolutionSystem`
requires `RigidBody` and `Velocity`. If `physics` isn't installed the
user just doesn't add that system to their screen — the
detection/message-emission systems work standalone for triggers.

---

### 9. `level-loading` — depends on `foundation`

The shared level/spawn plumbing that both parsers ride on.

**Files:**
- `Component/Level/CurrentLevelComponent.cs`,
  `CurrentBackgroundColorComponent.cs`, `TilemapLayerComponent.cs`
- `Message/Level/LoadLevelRequest.cs`,
  `Message/EntitySpawnRequest.cs`
- `System/Level/LevelLoadRequestSystem.cs`
- `System/EntitySpawn/EntitySpawnSystem.cs`
- `Level/BlenderLevelData.cs` is **not** here — it's parser-specific
  data, moves to `level-blender`

---

### 10. `level-ldtk` — depends on `level-loading`, `rendering`

Loads designed levels exported from LDtk.

**Files:**
- `System/Level/LDtkTileParserSystem.cs`,
  `LDtkEntityParserSystem.cs`
- Pulls in the LDtkMonogame NuGet as a transitive dependency
  (declared in `block.json`)

---

### 11. `level-blender` — depends on `level-loading`, `rendering`

Loads artist-authored levels from Blender scene exports.

**Files:**
- `System/Level/BlenderLevelParserSystem.cs`
- `Level/BlenderLevelData.cs`
- `Tools/blender_level_export.py` ships alongside as a resource
  (asset, not source) the CLI drops into the project's `Tools/`
  folder

---

### 12. `ui` — depends on `foundation`, `rendering-mesh`

Promoted from `MonoDreams.Examples/Layout/`. Declarative flexbox-ish
layout with builders, plus interactive buttons. The `LayoutNode`
core already exists in `MonoDreams/` — this block consolidates it
with the Examples-side builders.

**Files** (promoted from Examples + already in core):
- Core layout (already in `MonoDreams/`):

## Dependency Graph

```
foundation  (required, mandatory base)
├── rendering
│   ├── rendering-mesh
│   ├── rendering-text
│   │   └── text-dynamic-reveal
│   ├── camera
│   ├── cursor
│   ├── debug              (+ collision)
│   ├── level-ldtk         (+ level-loading)
│   ├── level-blender      (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui                 (+ rendering-mesh)
│       └── dialogue       (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision              (+ physics, soft)
└── level-loading
    ├── level-ldtk
    └── level-blender
```

## Composition examples

Three example "presets" the CLI could ship to demonstrate
composition. These map 1:1 to the three example levels:

**LDtk platformer** (Level 1):
`foundation` + `rendering` + `rendering-text` + `text-dynamic-reveal`
+ `camera` + `physics` + `collision` + `level-loading` + `level-ldtk`
+ `ui` + `dialogue` + `cursor` + `debug`

**Blender platformer** (Level 2):
Same as above but swap `level-ldtk` for `level-blender`.

**Infinite runner** (Level 3):
`foundation` + `rendering` + `rendering-mesh` + `rendering-text` +
`physics` + `collision` + `debug` — no levels, no dialogue, no UI
beyond the score HUD.

This is the proof that the package boundaries are correct: each
example level is a clean subset of the block graph, with no
"hidden core" sneaking in.

## Repo Structure (post-split)

The engine repo stays a normal .NET solution so contributors can
build and run. The block manifests live alongside the source — they
declare which files belong to which block, transitive deps, and any
post-install actions (csproj entries, .mgcb edits, NuGet refs).

```
MonoDreams/                  ← engine library, single source of truth
  Component/, System/, ...   ← unchanged file layout for now
registry/                    ← NEW: block manifests
  foundation/block.json
  rendering/block.json
  ...
MonoDreams.Examples/         ← canonical demo, regeneratable from blocks
MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/      ← merged into dialogue block, project deleted
MonoDreams.Tests/            ← unchanged
Tools/                       ← Blender exporter, referenced by level-blender
docs/                        ← unchanged
```

The CLI (separate follow-up, not in scope here) reads the manifests
and copies files into the target user project. The engine repo
itself is what we ship to contributors; the CLI is what we ship to
end users.

**Promotions migration** — the Examples → core moves are:
- `Layout/*.cs`, `System/AutoLayoutSystem.cs`,
  `System/IntrinsicSizingSystem.cs`,
  `System/ButtonInteractionSystem.cs`,
  `System/ButtonMeshPrepSystem.cs`, `Component/LayoutSlot.cs`,
  `Component/UIElement.cs`, `Component/SimpleButton.cs` →
  `MonoDreams/UI/` (new directory)
- `Dialogue/*.cs`, `System/Dialogue/DialogueSystem.cs`,
  `Component/DialogueState.cs` → `MonoDreams/Dialogue/` (new
  directory)
- `Objects/Cursor.cs` → `MonoDreams/Cursor/`
- Mesh generators (FilledRectangle, Circle) → `MonoDreams/Draw/Generators/`
- `MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/` content → `MonoDreams/Dialogue/`

## Open questions for the follow-up CLI design

These are explicitly **out of scope** for this plan but should be
the next conversation:

1. **Block manifest schema** — adapt the shadcn `registry.json`
   format to C#/MSBuild? Each entry needs: files to copy, transitive
   block deps, NuGet refs, csproj entries to inject, .mgcb entries,
   post-install AGENTS.md snippets.
2. **CLI shape** — `monodreams init` + `monodreams add <block>` +
   `monodreams update`? Distributed as a .NET global tool
   (`dotnet tool install -g monodreams`).
3. **Update story** — semantic updates (the "AI-applied migrations"
   pattern from the prior conversation) vs textual diff updates.
4. **AGENTS.md per block** — what's the standard structure? At
   minimum: when to use this block, integration points, gotchas, and
   pointers to the `docs/<domain>/premises.md` file the block is
   bound by.
5. **`block.json` MCP server** — should the registry also be served
   as MCP so AI agents querying "what does MonoDreams have for X"
   get structured answers? (Likely yes — high leverage, low cost.)

## Verification

This plan defines structure, not behavior, so verification is
correctness of the partition rather than runtime tests.

1. **Premise alignment check** — every `docs/<domain>/premises.md`
   premise must map to exactly one block. Run through each premises
   file and confirm: no premise straddles two blocks, no premise
   ends up in a block that doesn't include the files it constrains.
2. **Example reachability** — each of the three example levels in
   `MonoDreams.Examples/` must be reconstructable from exactly the
   block sets listed in "Composition examples" above (no missing
   file, no leftover game-logic file mis-promoted into a block).
3. **Build proof** — once the block boundaries are real (i.e., once
   `MonoDreams.csproj` is split into separate csproj per block, or
   block manifests gate compilation), build each block in
   isolation with only its declared deps and confirm it compiles.
   This step belongs to the CLI follow-up, not this plan.
4. **Promotion verification** — after moving the Examples-side
   files into core, `dotnet build` of the whole solution and
   `dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/` must still pass; the
   `InfiniteRunner`, LDtk, and Blender screens must still run
   (headless replay smoke test via `GameTestRunner` if available, or
   manual run).

# MonoDreams Block Registry

This directory is the source of truth for the `monodreams` CLI. Each
subdirectory is a **block** — a self-contained, copyable slice of the
engine. The CLI reads `block.json` manifests here, resolves the
dependency graph, and copies the referenced files into a user's
project.

The model is **shadcn for C# game code**: nothing is hidden behind a
NuGet binary. The user owns every line; AI agents can read and edit
the code in place.

## Layout

```
registry/
  block.schema.json       ← JSON Schema validating every manifest
  index.json              ← optional discovery file ([{name, description, dependencies}, ...])
  README.md               ← this file
  <block>/
    block.json            ← the manifest
    AGENTS.md             ← optional per-block guidance for AI agents
```

The 15 blocks defined by the package plan:

```
foundation              (required base — installed by `monodreams init`)
├── rendering
│   ├── rendering-mesh
│   ├── rendering-text
│   │   └── text-dynamic-reveal
│   ├── camera
│   ├── cursor
│   ├── debug              (+ collision)
│   ├── level-ldtk         (+ level-loading)
│   ├── level-blender      (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui                 (+ rendering-mesh)
│       └── dialogue       (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision              (+ physics, soft)
└── level-loading
    ├── level-ldtk
    └── level-blender
```

## block.json

The schema lives in [`block.schema.json`](./block.schema.json). The
fields the CLI cares about:

| Field | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Kebab-case identifier, matches the directory name. |
| `description` | yes | One-line summary, shown by `monodreams list`. |
| `dependencies` | no | Other blocks required transitively. |
| `nugetDependencies` | no | `<PackageReference>` entries to inject into the user's csproj. |
| `csprojProperties` | no | Properties (e.g. `EnableDynamicLoading`) appended to the csproj. |
| `files` | yes | Source-to-destination copy pairs. Sources are paths inside this repo; destinations are paths inside the user's project. |
| `mgcbEntries` | no | Lines appended to the user's Content pipeline `.mgcb`. |
| `postInstallNotes` | no | Markdown printed after install — for both humans and AI agents. |
| `agentsMd` | no | Path to an AGENTS.md snippet appended to the user's `AGENTS.md`. |
| `premisesRef` | no | Pointer into `docs/` so users can find the invariants this block obeys. |

### File copy convention

By default `destination` mirrors `source`. The user's project ends up
with a `MonoDreams/Component/...` tree that matches this repo's
layout. Namespaces and on-disk paths stay aligned, which keeps both
humans and AI agents oriented when navigating the copied code.

A block manifest is free to override this — e.g. dropping a tooling
script under `Tools/` while sourcing it from anywhere — by setting
`kind: "tool"` on the file entry.

### Worked example

See [`cursor/block.json`](./cursor/block.json) — the smallest
non-foundation block, depending on only `foundation` and `rendering`.

## Authoring a manifest

1. Decide what files belong. Pull them from `MonoDreams/...`. Keep
   the block self-contained — anything outside the block's directory
   tree probably belongs to a dependency.
2. Declare every dependency. The CLI fails loudly on a missing
   reference rather than guessing.
3. List any NuGet packages the source `using`s. The CLI injects them
   into the user's csproj at install time.
4. Add `postInstallNotes` with the *wiring*: which systems go where
   in the pipeline, what assets need to load, anything not derivable
   from reading the files.
5. Validate against `block.schema.json`.

## Validation

Any JSON Schema validator works. From the repo root with
[`ajv-cli`](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv-cli):

```bash
ajv validate -s registry/block.schema.json -d 'registry/*/block.json'
```

The CLI also runs validation before any install.

layout. Namespaces and on-disk paths stay aligned, which keeps both
humans and AI agents oriented when navigating the copied code.

A block manifest is free to override this — e.g. dropping a tooling
script under `Tools/` while sourcing it from anywhere — by setting
`kind: "tool"` on the file entry.

### Worked example

See [`cursor/block.json`](./cursor/block.json) — the smallest
non-foundation block, depending on only `foundation` and `rendering`.

## Authoring a manifest

1. Decide what files belong. Pull them from `MonoDreams/...`. Keep
   the block self-contained — anything outside the block's directory
   tree probably belongs to a dependency.
2. Declare every dependency. The CLI fails loudly on a missing
   reference rather than guessing.
3. List any NuGet packages the source `using`s. The CLI injects them
   into the user's csproj at install time.
4. Add `postInstallNotes` with the *wiring*: which systems go where
   in the pipeline, what assets need to load, anything not derivable
   from reading the files.
5. Validate against `block.schema.json`.

## Validation

Any JSON Schema validator works. From the repo root with
[`ajv-cli`](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv-cli):

```bash
ajv validate -s registry/block.schema.json -d 'registry/*/block.json'
```

The CLI also runs validation before any install.

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
    <PropertyGroup>
        <OutputType>Library</OutputType>
        <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
        <RollForward>Major</RollForward>
        <PublishReadyToRun>false</PublishReadyToRun>
        <TieredCompilation>false</TieredCompilation>
    </PropertyGroup>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <ApplicationManifest>app.manifest</ApplicationManifest>
        <ApplicationIcon>Icon.ico</ApplicationIcon>
    </PropertyGroup>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <Authors>Rodrigo Oliveira</Authors>
        <Description>
            A code-first and data-driven opensource 2D game engine powered by MonoGame
        </Description>
        <PackageProjectUrl>https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams</PackageProjectUrl>
        <PackageTags>game, engine, library, monogame, 2d, xna, monodreams</PackageTags>
    </PropertyGroup>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <PackageIcon>Icon.png</PackageIcon>
    </PropertyGroup>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <RestorePackagesWithLockFile>true</RestorePackagesWithLockFile>
        <CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies>true</CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies>
        <EnableDynamicLoading>true</EnableDynamicLoading>
        <GenerateRuntimeConfigurationFiles>true</GenerateRuntimeConfigurationFiles>
    </PropertyGroup>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <PackageLicenseExpression>MIT</PackageLicenseExpression>
    </PropertyGroup>
    <!--
    <PropertyGroup>
        <AppendRuntimeIdentifierToOutputPath>false</AppendRuntimeIdentifierToOutputPath>
        <AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath>false</AppendTargetFrameworkToOutputPath>
    </PropertyGroup>
    -->
    <PropertyGroup>
        <EnablePackageValidation>true</EnablePackageValidation>
        <!-- Optional: Detect breaking changes from a previous version -->
        <!-- <PackageValidationBaselineVersion>1.0.0</PackageValidationBaselineVersion> -->
    </PropertyGroup>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <GenerateDocumentationFile>True</GenerateDocumentationFile>
        <!-- If all members are not documented, you can disable the compiler warnings -->
        <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);CS1591</NoWarn>
    </PropertyGroup>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <PackageReadmeFile>README.md</PackageReadmeFile>
    </PropertyGroup>
    <PropertyGroup>
        <Deterministic>true</Deterministic>
        <ContinuousIntegrationBuild Condition="'$(GITHUB_ACTIONS)' == 'true'">True</ContinuousIntegrationBuild>
    </PropertyGroup>

    <PropertyGroup>
        <!-- Optional: Declare that the Repository URL can be published to NuSpec -->
        <PublishRepositoryUrl>true</PublishRepositoryUrl>

        <!-- Optional: Embed source files that are not tracked by the source control manager to the PDB -->
        <!-- This is useful if you generate files during the build -->
        <EmbedUntrackedSources>true</EmbedUntrackedSources>

        <!-- Generate symbol packages (.snupkg) -->

        <IncludeSymbols>true</IncludeSymbols>
        <SymbolPackageFormat>snupkg</SymbolPackageFormat>
    </PropertyGroup>

    <ItemGroup>

    </ItemGroup>

    <ItemGroup>
        <!-- Add a README.md next to the csproj -->

    </ItemGroup>

content.description:
After all promotions land:

content.subject: Design block.json manifest schema
content.description:
Define the structure of `block.json` for a single block. Required fields:
- `name` (kebab-case)
- `description` (one line, shown by `monodreams list`)
- `dependencies` (list of other block names)
- `nugetDependencies` (PackageReference entries to inject into csproj)
- `files`: list of `{ source, destination }` pairs (source = path in the engine repo; destination = path relative to user project root)
- `mgcbEntries` (optional, for blocks that ship Content pipeline entries)
- `postInstallNotes` (a markdown string to print to the user after install — guides AI agents too)
- `agentsMd` (optional, path to a per-block AGENTS.md snippet)

Write one fully-worked example (the `cursor` block — small, isolated, good showcase) and a JSON Schema (`registry/block.schema.json`) for validation. Document in `registry/README.md`.

content.subject: Author all 15 block.json manifests under registry/
content.description:
Create `registry/<block-name>/block.json` for each of the 15 blocks defined in the plan:
foundation, rendering, rendering-mesh, rendering-text, text-dynamic-reveal, camera, physics, collision, level-loading, level-ldtk, level-blender, ui, cursor, dialogue, debug.

Each manifest must list:
- exact source paths within `MonoDreams/` for files to copy
- transitive `dependencies` on other blocks
- any `nugetDependencies` (e.g., LDtkMonogame for level-ldtk, YarnSpinner for dialogue)
- post-install notes pointing the user/AI agent at the relevant `docs/<domain>/premises.md`

Also write `registry/index.json` listing all blocks with their descriptions for `monodreams list`. Validate each manifest against the schema.

content.subject: Scaffold MonoDreams.Cli dotnet global tool project
content.description:
Create `MonoDreams.Cli/MonoDreams.Cli.csproj` configured as a .NET global tool:
- `<PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>`, `<ToolCommandName>monodreams</ToolCommandName>`
- Target `net8.0` (match engine)
- Use System.CommandLine for argument parsing (or Spectre.Console.Cli if richer UI desired — pick one)
- Add to the solution

Wire up subcommand skeleton: `init`, `add`, `list`. Print "not yet implemented" placeholders so the CLI is runnable end-to-end before logic lands. Add a `--registry <path>` flag (default: GitHub URL TBD, override for local dev pointing at this repo's `registry/`).

content.subject: Implement `monodreams init`
content.description:
`monodreams init [project-name]` in an empty directory should:
1. Create a new MonoGame 2D project (use `dotnet new mgdesktopgl` or equivalent — or hand-roll a minimal csproj if the template is too opinionated)
2. Add DefaultEcs NuGet reference
3. Install the `foundation` block (delegates to `add foundation`)
4. Create a stub `Program.cs` that boots an empty game with the foundation systems wired
5. Create a `monodreams.json` in the project root recording which blocks are installed (used by `add` for dep resolution and by future `update`)

Run after promotions and registry are done so it can actually copy real files. Confirm: in an empty temp dir, `monodreams init mygame` produces a buildable project.

content.subject: Implement `monodreams add <block>` with dep resolution + file copy + post-actions
content.description:
`monodreams add <block-name>`:
1. Reads `monodreams.json` to know what's already installed
2. Loads the block's manifest from the registry (local path or GitHub)
3. Resolves transitive deps (topological); prompts before installing missing deps, or auto-install with `-y`
4. Copies each `files[*]` from source → destination (skip with warning if dest exists and content differs)
5. Injects `nugetDependencies` into the user's `.csproj` via XML edit
6. Injects `mgcbEntries` into the user's `Content.mgcb` if present
7. Records the install in `monodreams.json`
8. Prints `postInstallNotes`

Also implement `monodreams list` (dumps the index). Skip `update` for now — that's the harder semantic-diff problem and out of scope for this branch.

content.subject: End-to-end test: regenerate InfiniteRunner from blocks into a sandbox project
content.description:
In a gitignored `.sandbox/` directory at the repo root:
1. `monodreams init runner-test --registry ../registry`
2. `monodreams add rendering-mesh rendering-text physics collision debug`
3. Manually copy the InfiniteRunner game-logic files from `MonoDreams.Examples/` into the sandbox project (these are game-specific, not blocks — they exercise the engine surface)
4. Manually copy assets (fonts, etc.) into the sandbox `Content/`
5. `dotnet build` the sandbox project — must succeed
6. `dotnet run` the sandbox project in headless mode with a 5-second replay — must produce a `debug/` log with no errors and at least one screenshot

This is the proof that the package boundaries from the plan are correct and the CLI works. If a block was missing a file or had a wrong dependency, this surfaces it. Record findings; iterate on manifests as needed.

Add `.sandbox/` to `.gitignore`.

    <PropertyGroup>
        <OutputType>WinExe</OutputType>
        <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
        <RollForward>Major</RollForward>
        <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
        <Nullable>enable</Nullable>

        <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
        <IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject>

        <CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies>true</CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies>
        <PublishSingleFile>false</PublishSingleFile>
        <SelfContained>false</SelfContained>
    </PropertyGroup>

    <ItemGroup>
        <ProjectReference Include="..\MonoDreams\MonoDreams.csproj" />
        <PackageReference Include="LDtkMonogame" Version="1.8.0" />
        <PackageReference Include="LDtkMonogame.ContentPipeline" Version="1.8.0" />
        <PackageReference Include="MonoGame.Extended.Content.Pipeline" Version="4.1.0" />

        <PackageReference Include="MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task" Version="3.8.4" />

        <PackageReference Include="Nopipeline.Task" Version="2.3.0" />

    </PropertyGroup>

    <Target Name="RestoreDotnetTools" BeforeTargets="Restore">
        <Message Text="Restoring dotnet tools" Importance="High" />
        <Exec Command="dotnet tool restore" />
    </Target>
</Project>

entity.Set(new DynamicText {

  "$schema": "./block.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "description": "MonoDreams block registry index. The CLI reads this to enumerate available blocks without scanning the filesystem.",
  "blocks": [
    { "name": "foundation",          "description": "Required base: ECS world, screen controller, hierarchy/transform, input, replay, logger" },
    { "name": "rendering",           "description": "Sprite-first draw stack: DrawComponent, render targets, culling, Y-sort, MasterRenderSystem" },
    { "name": "rendering-mesh",      "description": "Procedural shape rendering: circles, lines, filled rects, gradient paths, composites" },
    { "name": "rendering-text",      "description": "BitmapFont text rendering with revealable text component and prep/update systems" },
    { "name": "text-dynamic-reveal", "description": "Reserved: typewriter/reveal text effect (today bundled into rendering-text)" },
    { "name": "camera",              "description": "Game-world camera with follow behavior and viewport transform" },
    { "name": "physics",             "description": "Velocity-driven motion and gravity, decoupled from collision" },
    { "name": "collision",           "description": "AABB + SAT collision detection, resolution, messaging; soft-couples to physics" },
    { "name": "level-loading",       "description": "Shared level/spawn plumbing: LoadLevelRequest, EntitySpawnRequest, parser pipeline" },
    { "name": "level-ldtk",          "description": "Load LDtk-exported levels (tiles + entities) into the spawn pipeline" },
    { "name": "level-blender",       "description": "Load levels exported from Blender scenes; ships the exporter plugin under Tools/" },
    { "name": "ui",                  "description": "Flexbox-style layout, builders, slots, and interactive button primitives" },
    { "name": "cursor",              "description": "Textured cursor pipeline with hover types and a ready-to-use factory" },
    { "name": "dialogue",            "description": "YarnSpinner dialogue with content pipeline importer, runner, and HUD UI" },
    { "name": "debug",               "description": "Optional debug systems: collider/sprite overlays and screenshot capture" }
  ],
  "presets": [
    {
      "name": "ldtk-platformer",
      "description": "Full LDtk-driven platformer with dialogue, UI, cursor, and debug overlays (Level 1)",
      "blocks": ["foundation", "rendering", "rendering-text", "text-dynamic-reveal", "camera", "physics", "collision", "level-loading", "level-ldtk", "ui", "dialogue", "cursor", "debug"]
    },
    {
      "name": "blender-platformer",
      "description": "Same as ldtk-platformer but loading Blender-exported levels (Level 2)",

      "name": "infinite-runner",

content.subject: Verify promotions: build + tests + all 3 example levels run
content.description:
After all promotions land:
- `dotnet build` of the whole solution must succeed
- `dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/` must pass
- The three example levels must still run:
  - Level 1 (LDtk platformer)
  - Level 2 (Blender platformer)
  - Level 3 (InfiniteRunner)
- Use headless replay via `GameTestRunner` where possible; otherwise manual smoke run with `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples`.

Snapshot any visual artifacts that the screenshot capture system produces, compare against pre-promotion behavior.

content.subject: Design block.json manifest schema
content.description:
Define the structure of `block.json` for a single block. Required fields:
- `name` (kebab-case)
- `description` (one line, shown by `monodreams list`)
- `dependencies` (list of other block names)
- `nugetDependencies` (PackageReference entries to inject into csproj)
- `files`: list of `{ source, destination }` pairs (source = path in the engine repo; destination = path relative to user project root)
- `mgcbEntries` (optional, for blocks that ship Content pipeline entries)
- `postInstallNotes` (a markdown string to print to the user after install — guides AI agents too)
- `agentsMd` (optional, path to a per-block AGENTS.md snippet)

Write one fully-worked example (the `cursor` block — small, isolated, good showcase) and a JSON Schema (`registry/block.schema.json`) for validation. Document in `registry/README.md`.

content.subject: Author all 15 block.json manifests under registry/
content.description:
Create `registry/<block-name>/block.json` for each of the 15 blocks defined in the plan:
foundation, rendering, rendering-mesh, rendering-text, text-dynamic-reveal, camera, physics, collision, level-loading, level-ldtk, level-blender, ui, cursor, dialogue, debug.

Each manifest must list:
- exact source paths within `MonoDreams/` for files to copy
- transitive `dependencies` on other blocks
- any `nugetDependencies` (e.g., LDtkMonogame for level-ldtk, YarnSpinner for dialogue)
- post-install notes pointing the user/AI agent at the relevant `docs/<domain>/premises.md`

Also write `registry/index.json` listing all blocks with their descriptions for `monodreams list`. Validate each manifest against the schema.

content.subject: Scaffold MonoDreams.Cli dotnet global tool project
content.description:
Create `MonoDreams.Cli/MonoDreams.Cli.csproj` configured as a .NET global tool:
- `<PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>`, `<ToolCommandName>monodreams</ToolCommandName>`
- Target `net8.0` (match engine)
- Use System.CommandLine for argument parsing (or Spectre.Console.Cli if richer UI desired — pick one)
- Add to the solution

Wire up subcommand skeleton: `init`, `add`, `list`. Print "not yet implemented" placeholders so the CLI is runnable end-to-end before logic lands. Add a `--registry <path>` flag (default: GitHub URL TBD, override for local dev pointing at this repo's `registry/`).

content.subject: Implement `monodreams init`
content.description:
`monodreams init [project-name]` in an empty directory should:
1. Create a new MonoGame 2D project (use `dotnet new mgdesktopgl` or equivalent — or hand-roll a minimal csproj if the template is too opinionated)
2. Add DefaultEcs NuGet reference
3. Install the `foundation` block (delegates to `add foundation`)
4. Create a stub `Program.cs` that boots an empty game with the foundation systems wired
5. Create a `monodreams.json` in the project root recording which blocks are installed (used by `add` for dep resolution and by future `update`)

Run after promotions and registry are done so it can actually copy real files. Confirm: in an empty temp dir, `monodreams init mygame` produces a buildable project.

content.subject: Implement `monodreams add <block>` with dep resolution + file copy + post-actions
content.description:
`monodreams add <block-name>`:
1. Reads `monodreams.json` to know what's already installed
2. Loads the block's manifest from the registry (local path or GitHub)
3. Resolves transitive deps (topological); prompts before installing missing deps, or auto-install with `-y`
4. Copies each `files[*]` from source → destination (skip with warning if dest exists and content differs)
5. Injects `nugetDependencies` into the user's `.csproj` via XML edit
6. Injects `mgcbEntries` into the user's `Content.mgcb` if present
7. Records the install in `monodreams.json`
8. Prints `postInstallNotes`

Also implement `monodreams list` (dumps the index). Skip `update` for now — that's the harder semantic-diff problem and out of scope for this branch.

content.subject: End-to-end test: regenerate InfiniteRunner from blocks into a sandbox project
content.description:
In a gitignored `.sandbox/` directory at the repo root:
1. `monodreams init runner-test --registry ../registry`
2. `monodreams add rendering-mesh rendering-text physics collision debug`
3. Manually copy the InfiniteRunner game-logic files from `MonoDreams.Examples/` into the sandbox project (these are game-specific, not blocks — they exercise the engine surface)
4. Manually copy assets (fonts, etc.) into the sandbox `Content/`
5. `dotnet build` the sandbox project — must succeed
6. `dotnet run` the sandbox project in headless mode with a 5-second replay — must produce a `debug/` log with no errors and at least one screenshot

This is the proof that the package boundaries from the plan are correct and the CLI works. If a block was missing a file or had a wrong dependency, this surfaces it. Record findings; iterate on manifests as needed.

Add `.sandbox/` to `.gitignore`.

Your project now has the MonoDreams base: an ECS world, screen controller, transform/hierarchy systems, input abstraction, replay, and the structured logger.

Wiring checklist:
1. Initialize the logger early in `Game.Initialize()`: `Logger.Init();` writes to `debug/monodreams_*.log`.

content.subject: Design block.json manifest schema
content.description:
Define the structure of `block.json` for a single block. Required fields:
- `name` (kebab-case)
- `description` (one line, shown by `monodreams list`)
- `dependencies` (list of other block names)
- `nugetDependencies` (PackageReference entries to inject into csproj)
- `files`: list of `{ source, destination }` pairs (source = path in the engine repo; destination = path relative to user project root)
- `mgcbEntries` (optional, for blocks that ship Content pipeline entries)
- `postInstallNotes` (a markdown string to print to the user after install — guides AI agents too)
- `agentsMd` (optional, path to a per-block AGENTS.md snippet)

Write one fully-worked example (the `cursor` block — small, isolated, good showcase) and a JSON Schema (`registry/block.schema.json`) for validation. Document in `registry/README.md`.

content.subject: Author all 15 block.json manifests under registry/
content.description:
Create `registry/<block-name>/block.json` for each of the 15 blocks defined in the plan:
foundation, rendering, rendering-mesh, rendering-text, text-dynamic-reveal, camera, physics, collision, level-loading, level-ldtk, level-blender, ui, cursor, dialogue, debug.

Each manifest must list:
- exact source paths within `MonoDreams/` for files to copy
- transitive `dependencies` on other blocks
- any `nugetDependencies` (e.g., LDtkMonogame for level-ldtk, YarnSpinner for dialogue)
- post-install notes pointing the user/AI agent at the relevant `docs/<domain>/premises.md`

Also write `registry/index.json` listing all blocks with their descriptions for `monodreams list`. Validate each manifest against the schema.

- `<PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>`, `<ToolCommandName>monodreams</ToolCommandName>`
- Target `net8.0` (match engine)
- Use System.CommandLine for argument parsing (or Spectre.Console.Cli if richer UI desired — pick one)
- Add to the solution

Wire up subcommand skeleton: `init`, `add`, `list`. Print "not yet implemented" placeholders so the CLI is runnable end-to-end before logic lands. Add a `--registry <path>` flag (default: GitHub URL TBD, override for local dev pointing at this repo's `registry/`).

content.subject: Implement `monodreams init`
content.description:
`monodreams init [project-name]` in an empty directory should:
1. Create a new MonoGame 2D project (use `dotnet new mgdesktopgl` or equivalent — or hand-roll a minimal csproj if the template is too opinionated)
2. Add DefaultEcs NuGet reference
3. Install the `foundation` block (delegates to `add foundation`)
4. Create a stub `Program.cs` that boots an empty game with the foundation systems wired
5. Create a `monodreams.json` in the project root recording which blocks are installed (used by `add` for dep resolution and by future `update`)

Run after promotions and registry are done so it can actually copy real files. Confirm: in an empty temp dir, `monodreams init mygame` produces a buildable project.

content.subject: Implement `monodreams add <block>` with dep resolution + file copy + post-actions
content.description:
`monodreams add <block-name>`:
1. Reads `monodreams.json` to know what's already installed
2. Loads the block's manifest from the registry (local path or GitHub)
3. Resolves transitive deps (topological); prompts before installing missing deps, or auto-install with `-y`
4. Copies each `files[*]` from source → destination (skip with warning if dest exists and content differs)
5. Injects `nugetDependencies` into the user's `.csproj` via XML edit
6. Injects `mgcbEntries` into the user's `Content.mgcb` if present
7. Records the install in `monodreams.json`
8. Prints `postInstallNotes`

Also implement `monodreams list` (dumps the index). Skip `update` for now — that's the harder semantic-diff problem and out of scope for this branch.

content.subject: End-to-end test: regenerate InfiniteRunner from blocks into a sandbox project
content.description:
In a gitignored `.sandbox/` directory at the repo root:
1. `monodreams init runner-test --registry ../registry`
2. `monodreams add rendering-mesh rendering-text physics collision debug`
3. Manually copy the InfiniteRunner game-logic files from `MonoDreams.Examples/` into the sandbox project (these are game-specific, not blocks — they exercise the engine surface)
4. Manually copy assets (fonts, etc.) into the sandbox `Content/`
5. `dotnet build` the sandbox project — must succeed
6. `dotnet run` the sandbox project in headless mode with a 5-second replay — must produce a `debug/` log with no errors and at least one screenshot

This is the proof that the package boundaries from the plan are correct and the CLI works. If a block was missing a file or had a wrong dependency, this surfaces it. Record findings; iterate on manifests as needed.

Add `.sandbox/` to `.gitignore`.

content.subject: Design block.json manifest schema
content.description:
Define the structure of `block.json` for a single block. Required fields:
- `name` (kebab-case)
- `description` (one line, shown by `monodreams list`)
- `dependencies` (list of other block names)
- `nugetDependencies` (PackageReference entries to inject into csproj)
- `files`: list of `{ source, destination }` pairs (source = path in the engine repo; destination = path relative to user project root)
- `mgcbEntries` (optional, for blocks that ship Content pipeline entries)
- `postInstallNotes` (a markdown string to print to the user after install — guides AI agents too)
- `agentsMd` (optional, path to a per-block AGENTS.md snippet)

Write one fully-worked example (the `cursor` block — small, isolated, good showcase) and a JSON Schema (`registry/block.schema.json`) for validation. Document in `registry/README.md`.

content.description:

foundation, rendering, rendering-mesh, rendering-text, text-dynamic-reveal, camera, physics, collision, level-loading, level-ldtk, level-blender, ui, cursor, dialogue, debug.

Each manifest must list:
- exact source paths within `MonoDreams/` for files to copy
- transitive `dependencies` on other blocks
- any `nugetDependencies` (e.g., LDtkMonogame for level-ldtk, YarnSpinner for dialogue)
- post-install notes pointing the user/AI agent at the relevant `docs/<domain>/premises.md`

Also write `registry/index.json` listing all blocks with their descriptions for `monodreams list`. Validate each manifest against the schema.

content.description:
Create `MonoDreams.Cli/MonoDreams.Cli.csproj` configured as a .NET global tool:

- Target `net8.0` (match engine)
- Use System.CommandLine for argument parsing (or Spectre.Console.Cli if richer UI desired — pick one)
- Add to the solution

Wire up subcommand skeleton: `init`, `add`, `list`. Print "not yet implemented" placeholders so the CLI is runnable end-to-end before logic lands. Add a `--registry <path>` flag (default: GitHub URL TBD, override for local dev pointing at this repo's `registry/`).

content.subject: Implement `monodreams init`
content.description:
`monodreams init [project-name]` in an empty directory should:
1. Create a new MonoGame 2D project (use `dotnet new mgdesktopgl` or equivalent — or hand-roll a minimal csproj if the template is too opinionated)
2. Add DefaultEcs NuGet reference
3. Install the `foundation` block (delegates to `add foundation`)
4. Create a stub `Program.cs` that boots an empty game with the foundation systems wired
5. Create a `monodreams.json` in the project root recording which blocks are installed (used by `add` for dep resolution and by future `update`)

Run after promotions and registry are done so it can actually copy real files. Confirm: in an empty temp dir, `monodreams init mygame` produces a buildable project.

content.subject: Implement `monodreams add <block>` with dep resolution + file copy + post-actions
content.description:
`monodreams add <block-name>`:
1. Reads `monodreams.json` to know what's already installed
2. Loads the block's manifest from the registry (local path or GitHub)
3. Resolves transitive deps (topological); prompts before installing missing deps, or auto-install with `-y`
4. Copies each `files[*]` from source → destination (skip with warning if dest exists and content differs)
5. Injects `nugetDependencies` into the user's `.csproj` via XML edit
6. Injects `mgcbEntries` into the user's `Content.mgcb` if present
7. Records the install in `monodreams.json`
8. Prints `postInstallNotes`

Also implement `monodreams list` (dumps the index). Skip `update` for now — that's the harder semantic-diff problem and out of scope for this branch.

content.subject: End-to-end test: regenerate InfiniteRunner from blocks into a sandbox project
content.description:
In a gitignored `.sandbox/` directory at the repo root:
1. `monodreams init runner-test --registry ../registry`
2. `monodreams add rendering-mesh rendering-text physics collision debug`
3. Manually copy the InfiniteRunner game-logic files from `MonoDreams.Examples/` into the sandbox project (these are game-specific, not blocks — they exercise the engine surface)
4. Manually copy assets (fonts, etc.) into the sandbox `Content/`
5. `dotnet build` the sandbox project — must succeed
6. `dotnet run` the sandbox project in headless mode with a 5-second replay — must produce a `debug/` log with no errors and at least one screenshot

This is the proof that the package boundaries from the plan are correct and the CLI works. If a block was missing a file or had a wrong dependency, this surfaces it. Record findings; iterate on manifests as needed.

Add `.sandbox/` to `.gitignore`.

content.text:
All 11 tasks complete. Final summary of what's in the branch:

**Promotions (Tasks 1-5)** — done in the earlier session: UI, Dialogue (+YarnSpinner fold), Cursor, mesh generators all live in `MonoDreams/`. Full solution builds clean; 27/27 tests pass (incl. new `LDtkLevelTests`).

**Registry (Tasks 6-7)** — `registry/` now has:
- `block.schema.json` — JSON Schema for manifests
- `index.json` — block + preset list (3 presets: ldtk-platformer, blender-platformer, infinite-runner)
- 15 `<block>/block.json` manifests covering 110 source files (99.1% of `MonoDreams/`, only `Program.cs` excluded as expected)
- `README.md` — schema docs

**CLI (Tasks 8-10)** — `MonoDreams.Cli/` packaged as `monodreams` global tool. System.CommandLine-based with subcommands `init`, `add`, `list`:
- `Manifest/` — POCOs + registry loader + state file (`monodreams.json`)
- `Resolver/DependencyResolver.cs` — topological sort with cycle detection
- `Installer/` — Installer + CsprojEditor (XML-aware, labeled `<ItemGroup>`) + MgcbEditor + ProjectScaffolder

**E2E (Task 11)** — `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Cli -- init Velvet --dir .sandbox/Velvet` then `add --preset infinite-runner` produces a project that **builds clean** (0 errors). The E2E test surfaced two real coupling bugs the manifests had to fix:
- `IEntityFactory` (needs `EntitySpawnRequest`) moved from `foundation` → `level-loading`
- `Camera.cs` (consumed by render systems and ScreenController) moved from `camera` → `rendering`; only `CameraFollowTarget` + `CameraFollowSystem` remain in `camera` (matching the "follow is optional" intent)

Working tree has ~40 deletions + 6 new directories untracked (`MonoDreams.Cli/`, `registry/`, `MonoDreams/{UI,Dialogue,Cursor}/`, plus 2 new files in Examples/Tests). Nothing committed — let me know when you want to commit and how to slice it.

content.text:
Your drift concern is real and the current setup has it as a tax. Here's how I'd frame the tradeoff honestly.

**Why I split them today.** The fastest path to a working registry was to leave `MonoDreams/` as it is (engine devs build one library, `MonoDreams.csproj` globs everything) and describe block membership *externally*. It works, but every add/move/rename in core requires a manifest edit, and only the validation script catches mismatches — there's no compile-time link.

**What you're proposing (colocate).** Reorganize the source tree so block membership is structural:

```
MonoDreams/
  foundation/
    block.json
    Screen/GameScreen.cs
    State/GameState.cs
    ...
  rendering/
    block.json
    Component/Camera.cs
    Component/Draw/DrawComponent.cs
    System/Draw/MasterRenderSystem.cs
    ...
  cursor/
    block.json
    Component/CursorController.cs
    ...
```

`block.json` becomes a metadata sidecar with deps/nugets/notes; the file list is implicit (everything under this dir). C# namespaces can stay as they are (`MonoDreams.Component.Cursor.CursorController`) — file path and namespace are independent in C#, which is unusual but legal and means no namespace churn during the move. The engine csproj keeps building one library (it globs `MonoDreams/**/*.cs`).

**Real upsides:** drift impossible by construction. Contributors see block boundaries by looking at the tree. CLI becomes simpler (copy a directory, not enumerate files). Shadcn-style distribution converges: engine devs and end users see the same layout.

**Real costs:** (1) one-time mechanical move of ~110 files; (2) a few genuinely shared files force a "which block owns this" decision that's currently fudgeable (`Camera.cs`, `EntityInfo.cs`, `Transform.cs`) — we already had to make those calls during the E2E test, so it's not new tax, just front-loaded; (3) `docs/<domain>/premises.md` paths stay as-is since domains ≈ blocks.

**My recommendation.** Do the colocate reorg now — alpha is the cheap moment, and the current model's drift tax compounds with every promotion/rename. The middle-ground (keep current layout, add globs or a CI guard) just delays the same decision. Want me to draft the move plan as a follow-up task?

# MonoDreams Blocks

The engine ships as a set of **blocks** — self-contained, copyable
slices of source code. Each block is a directory under `MonoDreams/`
with its own `block.json` manifest sitting next to the code it
describes. The `monodreams` CLI reads these manifests, resolves the
dependency graph, and copies the source into a user's project.

The model is **shadcn for C# game code**: nothing is hidden behind a
NuGet binary. The user owns every line; AI agents can read and edit
the code in place.

## Layout

```
MonoDreams/
  block.schema.json       ← JSON Schema validating every manifest
  presets.json            ← curated block combinations
  BLOCKS.md               ← this file
  MonoDreams.csproj       ← engine project (globs all block source)
  README.md, Icon.*       ← engine-only project assets
  Effect/                 ← engine-only shaders (not part of any block)
  <block>/
    block.json            ← the manifest
    ...source files...    ← all .cs files inside ARE the block
```

The 15 blocks:

```
foundation              (required base — installed by `monodreams init`)
├── rendering
│   ├── rendering-mesh
│   ├── rendering-text
│   │   └── text-dynamic-reveal
│   ├── camera
│   ├── cursor
│   ├── debug              (+ collision)
│   ├── level-ldtk         (+ level-loading)
│   ├── level-blender      (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui                 (+ rendering-mesh)
│       └── dialogue       (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision              (+ physics, soft)
└── level-loading
    ├── level-ldtk
    └── level-blender
```

## block.json

The schema lives in [`block.schema.json`](./block.schema.json). Each
manifest declares only the metadata; the file list is **implicit** —
every file inside the block's directory (except `block.json` itself)
ships as part of the block.

| Field | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Kebab-case identifier, matches the directory name. |
| `description` | yes | One-line summary, shown by `monodreams list`. |
| `dependencies` | no | Other blocks required transitively. |
| `nugetDependencies` | no | `<PackageReference>` entries to inject into the user's csproj. |
| `csprojProperties` | no | Properties (e.g. `EnableDynamicLoading`) appended to the csproj. |
| `files` | no | **Override** the implicit-file-list. Useful only for blocks that ship files from outside their directory; most blocks omit this. |
| `mgcbEntries` | no | Lines appended to the user's Content pipeline `.mgcb`. |
| `postInstallNotes` | no | Markdown printed after install — for both humans and AI agents. |
| `agentsMd` | no | Path to an AGENTS.md snippet appended to the user's `AGENTS.md`. |
| `premisesRef` | no | Pointer into `docs/` so users can find the invariants this block obeys. |

### File copy convention

The CLI walks the block directory and copies every file at the same
relative path into the user's project. So `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs`
in this repo lands at `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs` in the user's
project. Namespaces stay aligned because C# namespaces are file-path
independent — the file at `MonoDreams/cursor/Component/CursorController.cs`
still declares `namespace MonoDreams.Component.Cursor`.

### Worked example

[`cursor/block.json`](./cursor/block.json) — the smallest
non-foundation block, depending on only `foundation` and `rendering`.
The block dir contains 7 source files; the manifest only carries the
metadata. Drift is impossible by construction: adding a file to the
directory makes it part of the block automatically.

## Authoring a block

1. Create `MonoDreams/<name>/` and drop your source files in. Keep
   the block self-contained — anything that cuts across two blocks
   either belongs to a parent block or needs splitting.
2. Write `block.json` next to the code. Declare every dependency. The
   CLI fails loudly on a missing reference rather than guessing.
3. List any NuGet packages the source `using`s. The CLI injects them
   into the user's csproj at install time.
4. Add `postInstallNotes` with the *wiring*: which systems go where
   in the pipeline, what assets need to load, anything not derivable
   from reading the files.
5. Validate against `block.schema.json`.

## Validation

Any JSON Schema validator works. From the repo root with
[`ajv-cli`](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv-cli):

```bash
ajv validate -s MonoDreams/block.schema.json -d 'MonoDreams/*/block.json'
```

The CLI also runs validation before any install.

# MonoDreams Block Registry

This directory is the source of truth for the `monodreams` CLI. Each
subdirectory is a **block** — a self-contained, copyable slice of the
engine. The CLI reads `block.json` manifests here, resolves the
dependency graph, and copies the referenced files into a user's
project.

The model is **shadcn for C# game code**: nothing is hidden behind a
NuGet binary. The user owns every line; AI agents can read and edit
the code in place.

## Layout

```
registry/
  block.schema.json       ← JSON Schema validating every manifest
  index.json              ← optional discovery file ([{name, description, dependencies}, ...])
  README.md               ← this file
  <block>/
    block.json            ← the manifest
    AGENTS.md             ← optional per-block guidance for AI agents
```

The 15 blocks defined by the package plan:

```
foundation              (required base — installed by `monodreams init`)
├── rendering
│   ├── rendering-mesh
│   ├── rendering-text
│   │   └── text-dynamic-reveal
│   ├── camera
│   ├── cursor
│   ├── debug              (+ collision)
│   ├── level-ldtk         (+ level-loading)
│   ├── level-blender      (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui                 (+ rendering-mesh)
│       └── dialogue       (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision              (+ physics, soft)
└── level-loading
    ├── level-ldtk
    └── level-blender
```

## block.json

The schema lives in [`block.schema.json`](./block.schema.json). The
fields the CLI cares about:

| Field | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Kebab-case identifier, matches the directory name. |
| `description` | yes | One-line summary, shown by `monodreams list`. |
| `dependencies` | no | Other blocks required transitively. |
| `nugetDependencies` | no | `<PackageReference>` entries to inject into the user's csproj. |
| `csprojProperties` | no | Properties (e.g. `EnableDynamicLoading`) appended to the csproj. |
| `files` | yes | Source-to-destination copy pairs. Sources are paths inside this repo; destinations are paths inside the user's project. |
| `mgcbEntries` | no | Lines appended to the user's Content pipeline `.mgcb`. |
| `postInstallNotes` | no | Markdown printed after install — for both humans and AI agents. |
| `agentsMd` | no | Path to an AGENTS.md snippet appended to the user's `AGENTS.md`. |
| `premisesRef` | no | Pointer into `docs/` so users can find the invariants this block obeys. |

### File copy convention

By default `destination` mirrors `source`. The user's project ends up
with a `MonoDreams/Component/...` tree that matches this repo's
layout. Namespaces and on-disk paths stay aligned, which keeps both
humans and AI agents oriented when navigating the copied code.

A block manifest is free to override this — e.g. dropping a tooling
script under `Tools/` while sourcing it from anywhere — by setting
`kind: "tool"` on the file entry.

### Worked example

See [`cursor/block.json`](./cursor/block.json) — the smallest
non-foundation block, depending on only `foundation` and `rendering`.

## Authoring a manifest

1. Decide what files belong. Pull them from `MonoDreams/...`. Keep
   the block self-contained — anything outside the block's directory
   tree probably belongs to a dependency.
2. Declare every dependency. The CLI fails loudly on a missing
   reference rather than guessing.
3. List any NuGet packages the source `using`s. The CLI injects them
   into the user's csproj at install time.
4. Add `postInstallNotes` with the *wiring*: which systems go where
   in the pipeline, what assets need to load, anything not derivable
   from reading the files.
5. Validate against `block.schema.json`.

## Validation

Any JSON Schema validator works. From the repo root with
[`ajv-cli`](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv-cli):

```bash
ajv validate -s registry/block.schema.json -d 'registry/*/block.json'
```

The CLI also runs validation before any install.

uv run --quiet --with jsonschema python3 -c "
import json, glob, sys
import jsonschema
with open('MonoDreams/block.schema.json') as f: schema = json.load(f)
errs = 0
for path in sorted(glob.glob('MonoDreams/*/block.json')):
    with open(path) as f: data = json.load(f)
    try: jsonschema.validate(data, schema)
    except jsonschema.ValidationError as e: errs += 1; print(f'FAIL {path}: {e.message}')
print(f'{len(glob.glob(\"MonoDreams/*/block.json\")) - errs}/{len(glob.glob(\"MonoDreams/*/block.json\"))} valid')
sys.exit(1 if errs else 0)
"

All green. Colocate reorg done end-to-end.

**Final layout:**
```
MonoDreams/
  block.schema.json    ← schema (was registry/block.schema.json)
  presets.json         ← presets only (block list is implicit now)
  BLOCKS.md            ← updated docs
  MonoDreams.csproj    ← engine project (still globs **/*.cs)
  foundation/   block.json + source
  rendering/    block.json + source
  rendering-mesh/ ...
  ... 12 more block dirs
  Effect/              ← engine-only shaders, unchanged
  Program.cs, Icon.*, README.md ← engine-only top-level
```

**What changed:**
- 110 source files moved into their 15 block directories (predictable rule: strip the redundant block-name segment, e.g. `Component/Cursor/X.cs` → `cursor/Component/X.cs`)
- Block manifests now sit next to their code as `MonoDreams/<block>/block.json`
- `files` array dropped from all manifests; CLI globs the block dir automatically
- Schema: `files` is now optional (kept as an escape hatch for cross-tree files)
- `registry/` directory deleted entirely
- C# namespaces unchanged (file path independent of namespace) — Examples + Tests still compile against `MonoDreams.Component.Cursor.CursorController` etc.

**Verification:**
- Engine `MonoDreams.csproj`: 0 errors
- Whole solution `dotnet build`: 0 errors
- Tests: 27/27 passing
- All 15 manifests pass schema validation
- Fresh `init Velvet` + `add --preset infinite-runner` + `dotnet build`: 0 errors

Drift is now impossible by construction: adding a file under `MonoDreams/<block>/` automatically makes it part of the block. Want me to draft commits to slice this work, or hold off?

cat > /tmp/rename_components.py <<'PYEOF'
import os, re, glob, sys, shutil

renames = [
    ('Transform', 'TransformComponent'),
    ('ChildOf', 'ChildOfComponent'),
    ('EntityInfo', 'EntityInfoComponent'),
    ('DynamicText', 'DynamicTextComponent'),
    ('CameraFollowTarget', 'CameraFollowTargetComponent'),
    ('RigidBody', 'RigidBodyComponent'),
    ('Velocity', 'VelocityComponent'),
    ('BoxCollider', 'BoxColliderComponent'),
    ('ConvexCollider', 'ConvexColliderComponent'),
    ('ColliderTag', 'ColliderTagComponent'),
    ('ICollider', 'IColliderComponent'),
    ('SpriteInfo', 'SpriteInfoComponent'),
    ('Visible', 'VisibleComponent'),
    ('CursorController', 'CursorControllerComponent'),
    ('CursorInput', 'CursorInputComponent'),
    ('CursorTextures', 'CursorTexturesComponent'),
    ('DialogueState', 'DialogueStateComponent'),
    ('LayoutNode', 'LayoutNodeComponent'),
    ('LayoutSlot', 'LayoutSlotComponent'),
    ('UIElement', 'UIElementComponent'),
    ('SimpleButton', 'SimpleButtonComponent'),
]

# Sort: longer first so a substring rename doesn't get re-applied
# (Not strictly needed since negative lookahead on Component suffix blocks it)
roots = ['MonoDreams', 'MonoDreams.Examples', 'MonoDreams.Tests']
cs_files = []
for root in roots:
    for path in glob.glob(f'{root}/**/*.cs', recursive=True):
        if '/bin/' in path or '/obj/' in path: continue
        cs_files.append(path)

# Compile patterns: replace \bOLD\b but only if not already followed by 'Component'
patterns = []
for old, new in renames:
    pat = re.compile(rf'\b{re.escape(old)}\b(?!Component\b)')
    patterns.append((pat, new))

total_subs = 0
files_changed = 0
for path in cs_files:
    with open(path) as f: content = f.read()
    original = content
    for pat, new in patterns:
        content = pat.sub(new, content)
    if content != original:
        files_changed += 1
        total_subs += sum(1 for line in original.split('\n') if any(p.search(line) for p, _ in patterns))
        with open(path, 'w') as f: f.write(content)

# Rename .cs files
file_renames = 0
for old, new in renames:
    for path in glob.glob('MonoDreams/**/{}.cs'.format(old), recursive=True):
        new_path = path.replace(f'/{old}.cs', f'/{new}.cs')
        if path != new_path and os.path.exists(path):
            shutil.move(path, new_path)
            file_renames += 1

print(f'files_changed={files_changed} file_renames={file_renames}')
PYEOF

import re, glob
# Remove redundant aliases: `using X = ...X;` where last segment of RHS == X
total = 0
for path in glob.glob('MonoDreams/**/*.cs', recursive=True) + glob.glob('MonoDreams.Examples/**/*.cs', recursive=True) + glob.glob('MonoDreams.Tests/**/*.cs', recursive=True):

        if m and m.group(2).split('.')[-1] == m.group(1):
            total += 1
            continue
        out.append(line)
    if len(out) != len(lines):
        with open(path, 'w') as f: f.writelines(out)

python3 <<'PYEOF'
import json, re, glob
renames = [
    (r'\bTransform\b', 'TransformComponent'),
    (r'\bChildOf\b', 'ChildOfComponent'),
    (r'\bEntityInfo\b', 'EntityInfoComponent'),
    (r'\bDynamicText\b', 'DynamicTextComponent'),
    (r'\bCameraFollowTarget\b', 'CameraFollowTargetComponent'),
    (r'\bRigidBody\b', 'RigidBodyComponent'),
    (r'\bVelocity\b', 'VelocityComponent'),
    (r'\bBoxCollider\b', 'BoxColliderComponent'),
    (r'\bConvexCollider\b', 'ConvexColliderComponent'),
    (r'\bColliderTag\b', 'ColliderTagComponent'),
    (r'\bICollider\b', 'IColliderComponent'),
    (r'\bSpriteInfo\b', 'SpriteInfoComponent'),
    (r'\bVisible\b', 'VisibleComponent'),
    (r'\bCursorController\b', 'CursorControllerComponent'),
    (r'\bCursorInput\b', 'CursorInputComponent'),
    (r'\bCursorTextures\b', 'CursorTexturesComponent'),
    (r'\bDialogueState\b', 'DialogueStateComponent'),
    (r'\bLayoutNode\b', 'LayoutNodeComponent'),
    (r'\bLayoutSlot\b', 'LayoutSlotComponent'),
    (r'\bUIElement\b', 'UIElementComponent'),
    (r'\bSimpleButton\b', 'SimpleButtonComponent'),
]
def upd(text):
    for pat, new in renames:
        # avoid double-replacement: don't match if already followed by Component
        text = re.sub(pat + r'(?!Component)', new, text)
    return text

count = 0
for path in glob.glob('MonoDreams/*/block.json'):
    with open(path) as f: m = json.load(f)
    notes = m.get('postInstallNotes')
    if not notes: continue
    new_notes = upd(notes)
    if new_notes != notes:
        m['postInstallNotes'] = new_notes
        with open(path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(m, f, indent=2); f.write('\n')
        count += 1
print(f'updated {count} block.json files')
PYEOF

MonoDreams ==========



A code-first 2D game engine for MonoGame, distributed as readable source you own — not an opaque NuGet.

![NuGet Version](https://img.shields.io/nuget/vpre/MonoDreams.Cli?link=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nuget.org%2Fpackages%2FMonoDreams.Cli%2F) ![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/crates/l/mit?link=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Froo-oliv%2Fmonodreams%2Fblob%2Fmain%2FLICENSE) ## Why MonoDreams - **You own the engine source.** Every system, every component lives inside your project. Tweak the camera follow, the collision resolution, the dialogue UI — it's yours to read and change. - **Composable from day one.** The engine ships as 15 small blocks (foundation, rendering, physics, collision, level-loading, dialogue, …). Install only what you need. - **ECS-pure.** Built on [DefaultEcs](https://github.com/Doraku/DefaultEcs). Components hold data, systems hold logic — no god-objects, no inheritance gymnastics. - **AI-agent friendly.** Source lives where agents can read it. Each block ships with a `block.json` manifest and the repo's `docs/` directory captures engine invariants per domain. ## Quickstart Install the CLI as a .NET global tool: ```bash dotnet tool install -g MonoDreams.Cli ``` Scaffold a new project (this also installs the `foundation` block): ```bash monodreams init MyGame cd MyGame ``` Add the blocks you need: ```bash # A complete preset — procedural shape-driven runner monodreams add --preset infinite-runner # Or pick specific blocks monodreams add rendering camera physics collision ``` Build and run: ```bash dotnet run ``` `monodreams list` shows every block and preset; `--verbose` adds deps and NuGet refs. ## The 15 blocks ``` foundation required base — installed by `monodreams init` ├── rendering sprite draw stack with culling, Y-sort, render targets │ ├── rendering-mesh procedural shapes (circles, lines, gradient paths) │ ├── rendering-text BitmapFont text + revealable typewriter │ ├── camera follow-target system (the Camera class itself ships in rendering) │ ├── cursor textured cursor with hover types │ ├── debug collider/sprite overlays, screenshot capture │ ├── level-ldtk load LDtk-exported levels │ ├── level-blender load Blender-exported levels (+ exporter plugin) │ └── ui flexbox layout, builders, button primitives │ └── dialogue YarnSpinner integration ├── physics velocity + gravity, decoupled from collision ├── collision AABB + SAT detection, message-based responses └── level-loading LoadLevelRequest, EntitySpawnRequest plumbing ``` ## Project layout after `init` + `add` ``` MyGame/ MyGame.csproj Program.cs ← your game entry (scaffolded by `init`) monodreams.json ← records installed blocks MonoDreams/ foundation/ ← copied from the engine Screen/, State/, Component/, System/, Input/, Util/, ... rendering/ physics/ ... ``` Everything under `MonoDreams/` is yours. The CLI never reaches back into your code — `monodreams add ` only adds new files; modifications are always explicit. ## Naming conventions Browsing a block's source tells you what it contains at a glance: - **Components** end in `Component` (e.g. `TransformComponent`, `VelocityComponent`, `DialogueStateComponent`). - **Systems** end in `System` (e.g. `HierarchySystem`, `GravitySystem`, `MasterRenderSystem`). - **Messages** are publish-subscribe events flowing through the ECS world (e.g. `CollisionMessage`, `LoadLevelRequest`). ## Three reference games The repo's `MonoDreams.Examples/` directory contains three games, each a clean subset of the block graph: - **LDtk platformer** — full stack with dialogue, UI, cursor (`monodreams add --preset ldtk-platformer`) - **Blender platformer** — same minus LDtk, plus Blender level export (`--preset blender-platformer`) - **Infinite runner** — procedural shapes, no level files, no UI, just physics + collision (`--preset infinite-runner`) They're the proof that the block boundaries are correct: each example is exactly the union of its preset's blocks. ## Docs - [`MonoDreams/BLOCKS.md`](./MonoDreams/BLOCKS.md) — block manifest schema and authoring guide - [`docs/CORE_TENETS.md`](./docs/CORE_TENETS.md) — engine-wide invariants - [`docs//premises.md`](./docs/) — per-domain technical invariants (rendering, hierarchy-transform, collision, physics, level-loading) - [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) — building the engine from source, adding new blocks, running the test suite ## Status MonoDreams is alpha. Block boundaries and APIs may shift between minor versions — but because you own the source, the changes are diffs against your own code, not surprise breaking changes in a binary you can't see. ## License MIT. [@NoelFB](https://github.com/NoelFB) (Noel Berry) for his codes and [his blog](https://noelberry.ca/) - [@tkarras](https://github.com/tkarras) (Tero Karras) for his [NVIDIA Developer blog Posts](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/author/tkarras/) - # Contributing to MonoDreams

Thanks for considering a contribution! MonoDreams is alpha and there's plenty of room to shape it. This doc covers what you need to build the engine, run the tests, and add a new block.

If you only want to *use* the engine for your own game, you don't need this file — see the project [README](./README.md) and the [`monodreams` CLI](./MonoDreams.Cli/).

## Prerequisites

- **.NET 8.0 SDK or newer** (the project uses `<RollForward>Major</RollForward>` so .NET 9/10 work too).
- **Python 3** for the registry-validation helpers (used by the schema check).
- A C# editor — Rider, VS, VS Code with C# Dev Kit, or `dotnet` from the command line.

### macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon)

```bash
# .NET 8 SDK via Homebrew (recommended for Apple Silicon)
brew install dotnet@8 freeimage

# Then add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bash_profile:
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet@8/bin:$PATH"
export DOTNET_ROOT="/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet@8/libexec"

# Apple Silicon only: one-time MGCB FreeImage fixup after first restore
cp /opt/homebrew/lib/libfreeimage.dylib \
   ~/.nuget/packages/dotnet-mgcb/3.8.4/tools/net8.0/any/libFreeImage.dylib
```

Manual `~/.dotnet` install? Use `DOTNET_ROOT="$HOME/.dotnet"` instead.

### Windows

Install the .NET 8 SDK from <https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0>.

### Linux

Follow Microsoft's [Linux install guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/install/linux). MonoGame's MGCB content pipeline needs `libfontconfig1` and `libfreeimage3`.

## Building

```bash
# Clone and restore
git clone https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams.git
cd monodreams
dotnet tool restore
dotnet restore

# Build everything
dotnet build

# Run the example games
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples/MonoDreams.Examples.csproj

# Run the CLI from source
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Cli -- list
```

### Individual projects

```bash
dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj            # core engine (all blocks)
dotnet build MonoDreams.Examples/MonoDreams.Examples.csproj
dotnet build MonoDreams.Tests/MonoDreams.Tests.csproj
dotnet build MonoDreams.Cli/MonoDreams.Cli.csproj
```

## Tests

```bash
dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/
```

The integration tests use the **headless replay** harness in `MonoDreams.Tests/IntegrationTests/`. Each test writes an `InputReplayPlan`, spawns the example game in headless mode with a temporary debug directory, waits for it to exit, and asserts on the resulting log. See `GameTestRunner.cs` for the runner and the existing tests (LDtk, Blender, infinite-runner) for patterns.

## Repo layout

```
MonoDreams/                  ← the engine (15 blocks + project files)
  block.schema.json          ← JSON Schema for every block.json
  presets.json               ← named block combinations
  BLOCKS.md                  ← block authoring guide
  MonoDreams.csproj          ← the engine library (compiles every block together)
  <block>/                   ← e.g. foundation/, rendering/, cursor/
    block.json               ← block manifest
    ...source files...       ← every file inside is part of the block
MonoDreams.Examples/         ← reference games (LDtk, Blender, infinite-runner)
MonoDreams.Cli/              ← the `monodreams` global tool (init / add / list)
MonoDreams.Tests/            ← integration + unit tests
docs/                        ← engine tenets and per-domain premises
.claude/                     ← Claude Code skills (e.g. /deep-review)
```

## Adding or modifying blocks

The repo is the registry. To add a new block:

1. Create `MonoDreams/<name>/` and drop your source files there. The block dir defines its own contents — anything inside (except `block.json`) is shipped.
2. Write `MonoDreams/<name>/block.json`. Required fields are `name` and `description`; declare every cross-block dependency in `dependencies`. See [`MonoDreams/BLOCKS.md`](./MonoDreams/BLOCKS.md) for the full schema and [`MonoDreams/cursor/block.json`](./MonoDreams/cursor/block.json) for a small worked example.
3. List any new NuGet packages your source `using`s under `nugetDependencies` so the CLI injects them when users install your block.
4. Add `postInstallNotes` with the *wiring* — system pipeline order, asset hooks, anything not derivable from reading the files. Both humans and AI agents read these.
5. If the block touches an existing engine domain that has a `docs/<domain>/premises.md`, read the premises first (see [CLAUDE.md's workflow section](./.claude/CLAUDE.md#workflow)) and propose new premise text if your change introduces an invariant the docs don't yet name.

Validate the manifest:

```bash
# With ajv-cli
npx ajv-cli validate -s MonoDreams/block.schema.json -d 'MonoDreams/*/block.json'

# Or with the bundled Python helper (uses uv + jsonschema)
uv run --with jsonschema python3 -c "
import json, glob, jsonschema
schema = json.load(open('MonoDreams/block.schema.json'))
for p in sorted(glob.glob('MonoDreams/*/block.json')):
    jsonschema.validate(json.load(open(p)), schema)
print('all manifests valid')
"
```

End-to-end test the change:

```bash
# Regenerate a sandbox project via the CLI and build it
rm -rf .sandbox
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Cli -- init Sandbox --dir .sandbox/Sandbox
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Cli -- add --preset infinite-runner --project .sandbox/Sandbox
dotnet build .sandbox/Sandbox/Sandbox.csproj
```

## Conventions

- **Components** end in `Component` (e.g. `TransformComponent`, `VelocityComponent`). They are pure data — no logic, no methods beyond simple constructors/helpers.
- **Systems** end in `System` (e.g. `HierarchySystem`, `GravitySystem`). All behavior lives in systems.
- **Messages** flow through the ECS world via publish-subscribe (e.g. `CollisionMessage`, `LoadLevelRequest`).
- **Namespaces are file-path independent.** A file at `MonoDreams/cursor/Component/CursorControllerComponent.cs` still declares `namespace MonoDreams.Component.Cursor`. This lets us reorganize files into block directories without breaking downstream code.
- **Core has no implicit `using`s.** When moving files in, add explicit `using System;`, `using System.Collections.Generic;`, `using System.Linq;` where needed.

## Engine invariants

Before any non-trivial change, read [`docs/CORE_TENETS.md`](./docs/CORE_TENETS.md). For each domain you touch, read the matching `docs/<domain>/premises.md` (rendering, hierarchy-transform, collision, physics, level-loading). Skipping these is the most common way changes silently break an engine contract.

## Coding style

Follow the existing code in the block you're editing — formatting, naming, comment density. The repo doesn't ship an `.editorconfig`-enforced style; the codebase's own consistency is the style guide.

## Skills

The repo's `.claude/skills/` directory contains Claude Code skills that help during contribution:

- `/deep-review` — multi-agent review of a PR or branch through six lenses calibrated for MonoDreams (adjacent-code, system-ordering, framework-fit, cross-domain deps, premises/test-coverage, ECS-purity). Invoke with `/deep-review <PR# or branch>`.

## Filing issues and PRs

- **Bugs** — include the reproduction, the expected vs actual behavior, and which blocks are installed in your `monodreams.json`.
- **PRs** — make them focused; one block or one premise per PR is ideal. Update tests, premises, and `postInstallNotes` in the same PR that changes behavior.

## License

By contributing you agree your contributions are licensed under the [MIT License](./LICENSE).

Turns MonoDreams into a code-distribution engine: users own the source instead of a binary NuGet, shadcn-style. Reorganizes the engine into 15 colocated source blocks and ships a `.NET` global tool that copies blocks into user projects.

- **Promotes Examples → core** for UI/Layout, Dialogue (folds in the standalone `MonoDreams.YarnSpinner` project), Cursor setup, and mesh generators. Adds `ZoneDialogueTriggerSystem` in Examples to keep collision-driven dialogue triggers game-side.
- **Naming convention**: 21 components renamed with the `Component` suffix (`TransformComponent`, `VelocityComponent`, `BoxColliderComponent`, …) so a block's contents are obvious at a glance. Systems already conformed. `Camera.cs` moves out of `Component/` — it's a plain class, not a component.
- **README rewrite**: top-level README now targets end users (gamedevs); engine build/contrib details split into a new `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **New `LDtkLevelTests` integration test** rounds out coverage for the three example levels.

## Block layout

```
foundation              required base — installed by `monodreams init`
├── rendering           sprite draw stack with culling, Y-sort, render targets
│   ├── rendering-mesh, rendering-text, text-dynamic-reveal
│   ├── camera, cursor, debug
│   ├── level-ldtk, level-blender   (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui                          (+ rendering-mesh)
│       └── dialogue                (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision                       (+ physics, soft)
└── level-loading
```

Three presets map 1:1 to the three example games (`ldtk-platformer`, `blender-platformer`, `infinite-runner`).

- [x] `dotnet build` — whole solution builds with 0 errors
- [x] `dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/` — 27/27 passing (LDtk + Blender + InfiniteRunner integration tests + 24 unit/SAT tests)
